The day-level UK legal adoption instrument is The Companies, Partnerships and Groups (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/980), made 26 March 2015 and in force 6 April 2015. It substituted Companies Act 2006 section 405(2)(a)(iii) so that a trading company's group accounts must be drawn up 'in accordance with international accounting standards adopted pursuant to the IAS Regulation', and regulation 2(2) sets the application dates: financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2016, with the amended law optionally applied to a financial year beginning on or after 1 January 2015 if the directors so decide. This is the documented within-jurisdiction split that the v1.0 assessment flagged as the most valuable feature of the UK route: UK early adopters of IFRS 15 for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2015 coexist with mandatory adopters for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2016, inside one jurisdiction and one market, because the UK applied IFRS 15 as EU-adopted in July 2015, one year before the EU's deferred date of 1 January 2018. CAVEAT THAT MUST CARRY FORWARD (unchanged, from the canonical dossier): the early arm is voluntary, self-selected, mechanically correlated with the firm-level state the design conditions on, small in number, and publishes its first IFRS 15 statements together with their effect, so the diffusion clock has no window to run; the canonical dossier rejects this contrast as an IDENTIFICATION (V-009 Cycle-56, item 3). UK FILING-TIMESTAMP DETERMINATION (D-021, 2026-10-22): the FCA National Storage Mechanism's published glossary defines 'Publication date' as 'The date a document/announcement was released via a Regulatory Information Service (RIS) or uploaded to the NSM' and the Investor User Guide defines 'Filing date' as 'The date at which the information was made available for filing on the NSM' - both as DATES with no published time-of-day field (S-64, S-66). CONSEQUENCE: this UK row CANNOT be timed for the retrospective panel, because both UK transition windows (2016-01-01 and 2019-01-01) fall before the timestamp regime begins, whatever the answer to the remaining verification. The UK remains viable for PH-1, whose 2026-2027 window falls entirely after it. The NSM search API answered HTTP 403 from this environment on 2026-10-22, so whether a time component is exposed in the search response or CSV export could not be checked empirically; that is a failed retrieval, recorded as such, and the condition stays UNVERIFIED rather than false. The single remaining check is to run one NSM search for a known annual financial report and inspect the export header.
